slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single slot/copy covering the whole 512-byte EEPROM; no A/B selection. Validity decided by single-dword test FUN_08019a6c (0x08019a6c): equal -> apply branch FUN_080123fc (0x080123fc), not equal -> defaults branch (0x080123e4, FUN_0801241c 0x0801241c, 0x080123f0, 0x08012358). Header dword duplicated at 0x04/0x0c is the only redundancy; no backup copy or generation counter observed.

checksums.name: header_dword_equality (FUN_08019a6c) - candidate magic compare, not a checksum over payload
checksums.formula_detail: valid iff (*_DAT_08019a7c XOR _DAT_08019a80)==0, computed branchlessly as (-(x^c)|(x^c))>>0x1f on one dword of the 8-byte header copy installed by FUN_08019a3c. Which header word is compared (file offset 0x00 value 0x00000000 vs offset 0x04 value 0x62d00d60) is unresolvable from corpus (literal-pool values absent). No sum/XOR/CRC over any payload range exists in the 225 decompiled functions.

checksums.name: no_payload_checksum_found (exhaustive negative result)
checksums.formula_detail: Exhaustive Python sweep: all contiguous windows in 0x00-0x70 not overlapping header fields, under sum8/sum16/sum32 byte sums, LE/BE u16-word and u32-word sums, XOR-8/16/32, CRC32, Adler32, CRC16-CCITT-FALSE, FNV-1a-32, and per-8-byte-block reverse-bytes/reverse-u16/swap-u32 transforms. No non-self-referential match to stored 0x62d00d60. Example fixed ranges sav-00: 0x00-0x58 sum8=0x44 crc32=0x6dfe3116; 0x00-0x200 crc32=0xcb9e5aaf. Stored/computed below use CRC32 over 0x00-0x58 to document non-validation.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3 transfer driver (only toucher of 0x0D000000): programs source/dest/count+enable (0x80000000), programs WAITCNT-style register from config+6, busy-polls control high halfword, saves/restores enable global. Direction-agnostic; used for both EEPROM request-out and data-in phases. Register absolute addresses inferred as DMA3 0x040000D4/D8/DC (literal values absent from corpus).

EEPROM single-block (8-byte) serial read: bounds-checks block vs config ushort at +4, builds MSB-first request bitstream (address width = config byte at +8, two leading 1 bits), DMA-writes it to 0x0D000000 (len addr_bits+3), DMA-reads 0x44 halfwords back, unpacks 64 bits as 4x u16 stored to descending addresses at out+6..out+0. Returns 0 on success. Only caller of 0x0802c7fc; no write counterpart exists in corpus.

Bulk reader: loops blocks 0..63 (breaks if index>0x3f), dest+=8 per FUN_0802c87c call, stops on first error, returns (last_status==0). Fills 512 bytes at save_obj+4. Edge missed by callgraph.json (func_ tail-call alias in decompiled.c:2656/1217).

Loader/validator: fetch context id (0x0801d780), teardown (0x0801d9dc), bulk-read to param+4 (0x0802100c), conditional re-init (0x0801d69c), snapshot 8-byte header (0x08019a3c), on FUN_08019a6c failure install default header in validation global (0x08019a4c). Returns bulk-read success flag, not validity.

Constructor + top-level save consumer: initialises game object (sub-object via 0x0800dea0/0x0800d970, fields [0x29]=4 etc., zeroes +0x3e), stores back-pointer, then loads via 0x0801239c(global save obj); re-tests 0x08019a6c: valid -> 0x080123fc->0x08019a84 (empty stub), invalid -> 0x080123e4*, 0x0801241c, 0x080123f0*, 0x08012358* (*unrecovered entry points).
One-dword validity test: (-(g^c)|(g^c))>>0x1f, 0 iff global dword equals ROM constant _DAT_08019a80. Only integrity check in corpus. Callers found via decompiled text (callgraph lists none).
Copies exactly 2 u32 (8-byte header) from argument to validation global _DAT_08019a48. Used to snapshot loaded header and to install default header.
Installs ROM default header dwords _DAT_08019a64/_DAT_08019a68 into validation global via 0x08019a3c when validity test fails. RAM-only; no EEPROM write-back in corpus.
Defaults reset on invalid-save branch: writes ROM constant dword via 0x08019aac at *param, *param+100, *param+200, *param+300 (four fields 100 bytes apart). RAM-only in corpus.
Valid-save apply stub: only calls 0x08019a84(param2), which is an empty return. Real field deserialization not in corpus (unrecovered jumptable or direct RAM-image reads).
EEPROM timing setup wrapper: func_0x0802c684(4). Called once in boot (0x080222f8) before save load.
Timing/profile select: mode 4 stores _DAT_0802c69c to *_DAT_0802c698 (other modes write other globals). WAITCNT identity is hypothesis (literal values absent).

open_questions: Where is the EEPROM write (flush) driver and its callers? Absent from the 225-function corpus: only FUN_0802c87c calls the DMA3 driver FUN_0802c7fc, only for reads. Suspects: un-decompiled gap 0x080120b4-0x0801239c, unrecovered entry points 0x08012358/0x080123e4/0x080123f0, or code unexecuted during trace capture (no save action before frame 1058). Flush trigger, write granularity and header-rewrite behaviour unknown.

Which header dword does FUN_08019a6c (0x08019a6c) compare and what is ROM constant _DAT_08019a80: offset 0x04 value 0x62d00d60 (Reading A, candidate magic) or offset 0x00 value 0x00000000 (Reading B)? Literal-pool values (_DAT_08019a48/a64/a68/a7c/a80, _DAT_0800c330) are absent from decompiled.c; fuzz tests at offsets 0 and 4 discriminate behaviourally.

Absolute RAM address of the save object/image: proven only as save_obj+4 (image) with base from missing literal _DAT_0800c330. Blocks mapping FUN_0801241c +0/+100/+200/+300 dword resets to file offsets and any EWRAM (0x02xxxxxx) vs IWRAM (0x03xxxxxx) assignment.
Does any (unrecovered) code cross-check duplicated dwords at 0x04 vs 0x0c or test header halfwords at 0x08 (0xffff) / 0x0a? No such check in corpus.

Byte order: FUN_0802c87c stores each block's 4 unpacked u16s to descending RAM addresses - is .sav byte order equal to RAM order or per-block u16-reversed in RAM? Affects RAM-side offsets only; file offsets in this document are raw .sav offsets.

EEPROM config struct exact values: block-count ushort at +4 (>=64 proven by loop), address-width byte at +8 (expected 6 for 64 blocks), WAITCNT timing field at +6, error sentinel uRam0802c898, and FUN_0802c684 mode-4 stored value.
Semantics of (3,5) pair at 0x1c-0x1f (two u16_be-looking values / u8s at 0x1d,0x1f) and of zero payload 0x10-0x57; both snapshots predate gameplay divergence, later saves needed.

What wrote blocks 0x58-0x5f and bytes 0x65-0x67 (FF->00) between frames 1024-1058: game save-flush, EEPROM initialisation, or emulator backing-store behaviour? Sub-block change at 0x65 is not 8-byte aligned.

Is FUN_080123fc apply really a stub (FUN_08019a84 empty), with deserialization via direct RAM-image reads elsewhere (no traced per-field consumers beyond header), or hidden in unrecovered jumptable code?

Could a serializer exist among the 225 functions that only mutates the RAM image (save_obj+4) without touching 0x0D000000, indistinguishable from ordinary object code? FUN_0801241c/FUN_08019aac reset pattern is the only concrete lead; states/ contains only .ss.identity.json metadata, so paired-state reload verification was not possible in this workspace.
